source.title: Structural results on circular-arc graphs and circle graphs: A survey and the main open problems

accepted.question_text: Give forbidden induced subgraph characterizations for the full class of circular-arc graphs and for the full class of circle graphs. Work with simple graphs. An induced subgraph on a chosen vertex set keeps exactly the edges of the original graph whose endpoints both lie in that vertex set. A forbidden induced subgraph characterization asks for a set of graphs F such that a graph belongs to the target class exactly when it contains no induced graph from F. A circular-arc graph is an intersection graph of open arcs on a circle, and a circle graph is an intersection graph of chords on a circle.

evidence.quote: The main structural open problem regarding the classes of circular-arc graphs and circle graphs is that of characterizing them by forbidden induced subgraphs.

accepted.question_text: Give a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for those chordal graphs that are circular-arc graphs. Here a circular-arc graph is the intersection graph of a family of open arcs on a circle, a chordal graph is a graph with no induced cycle on four or more vertices, and a forbidden induced subgraph characterization specifies which induced subgraphs must be absent exactly for membership in the class.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Give a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for circular-arc graphs within the class of chordal graphs.

accepted.question_text: For every four-vertex graph H, characterize by forbidden induced subgraphs the circular-arc graphs within the class of H-free graphs. In this question, an H-free graph means a graph containing no induced subgraph isomorphic to H, and a circular-arc graph means an intersection graph of open arcs on a circle. The requested characterization should identify the induced obstructions that exactly separate circular-arc graphs from non-circular-arc graphs under the assumption that H is absent as an induced subgraph.
accepted.context_brief: Circular-arc graphs in H-free graph classes

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Give a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for circular-arc graphs within the class of H-free graphs where H is a four-vertex graph.

accepted.question_text: Characterize, by forbidden induced subgraphs, which claw-free graphs are circular-arc graphs. A claw is the complete bipartite graph K1,3, a claw-free graph contains no induced claw, and a circular-arc graph is an intersection graph of open arcs on a circle. As a starting subcase, determine the forbidden induced subgraph characterization for circular-arc graphs among graphs whose largest stable set has size at most two, where a stable set is a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices.

evidence.quote: characterize circular-arc graphs within the class of claw-free graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs.

accepted.question_text: Find a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for normal circular-arc graphs. A circular-arc graph is an intersection graph of open arcs on a circle, and it is normal when it has a circular-arc model in which no two arcs together cover the whole circle. The desired result should specify exactly which induced subgraphs are forbidden for a graph to admit such a normal circular-arc representation.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Find a characterization by forbidden induced subgraphs for normal circular-arc graphs.
The characterization of normal circular-arc graphs by minimal forbidden induced subgraphs is still open.

accepted.question_text: Find forbidden induced subgraph characterizations for Helly circular-arc graphs. A circular-arc graph is an intersection graph of open arcs on a circle; a Helly circular-arc graph is one having a circular-arc model in which every pairwise intersecting subfamily of arcs has a common point. The requested work includes both a minimal-forbidden-induced-subgraph characterization within the class of circular-arc graphs and a forbidden-induced-subgraph characterization that does not assume in advance that the input graph is circular-arc.

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Find a characterization by forbidden induced subgraphs for Helly circular-arc graphs.

accepted.question_text: For each nonnegative integer q, find a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for q-proper circular-arc graphs. A circular-arc graph is an intersection graph of open arcs on a circle. The term q-proper circular-arc graph is defined analogously to q-proper interval graphs: it should admit a circular-arc model in which any one arc is contained in at most q other arcs. The problem is to identify the induced obstructions that exactly characterize this restricted circular-arc model class.

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Find a characterization by forbidden induced subgraphs for q-proper circular-arc graphs.

accepted.question_text: Characterize, by forbidden induced subgraphs, which chordal graphs are circle graphs. A circle graph is the intersection graph of chords on a circle, and a chordal graph is a graph with no induced cycle on four or more vertices. The desired characterization should identify exactly which induced subgraphs prevent a chordal graph from being representable as a circle graph.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Characterize circle graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs within the class of chordal graphs.

accepted.question_text: Find a graph decomposition for Helly circle graphs under which the class of Helly circle graphs is closed, in analogy with the role of split decomposition for circle graphs. A circle graph is the intersection graph of chords on a circle. A Helly circle graph has a circle model whose pairwise different chords satisfy the Helly property: every pairwise intersecting set of chords has a common point. The goal is to identify a decomposition operation that preserves this Helly circle-graph class in the same structural way that split decomposition preserves circle graphs.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Find a decomposition such that Helly circle graphs are closed under this decomposition.

accepted.question_text: Characterize Helly circle graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs without assuming that the input graph is already a circle graph. A circle graph is the intersection graph of chords on a circle, and a Helly circle graph has a circle model with pairwise different chords such that every pairwise intersecting subset of chords has a common point. The desired result should list the induced obstructions whose absence is exactly equivalent to being a Helly circle graph.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Characterize Helly circle graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs.

accepted.question_text: Give a direct proof that graph complementation preserves circle graphs within bipartite graphs: if G is a bipartite graph and G is a circle graph, then the complement of G is also a circle graph. A circle graph is the intersection graph of chords on a circle. The proof should avoid deriving this corollary through Naji's theorem about the solvability over GF(2) of the associated system S(G).
accepted.context_brief: Direct proof of Bouchet's bipartite circle-graph corollary

evidence.quote: Also in [9], Bouchet posed the following problem: Is there a direct proof of Corollary 42?
